clue.text: Literary style apparent in mocking book

indicators.note: something apparent in another word shows up inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: to guy someone is to ridicule them, so mocking is guying
a writer's manner is their characteristic style

explanation.surface: A critic spots a particular writing style showing through in a satirical book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Literary' looks like the definition but belongs to the manner; the definition is the bare 'book', Walter Scott's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Guy Mannering is an 1815 novel by Sir Walter Scott, so it is an example of a book.

clue.text: Colour Marsh brought into sport

indicators.note: one piece is brought into another, placed inside it

parts.note: a game is a sport or contest
a bog is a marsh or swamp

explanation.surface: A painter adds colour to a scene of sport played on marshland.
explanation.definitionFit: Gamboge is a deep yellow pigment and the colour named after it.

clue.text: Length of time court's imposed

indicators.note: in a down clue, imposed means laid on top of, so the first piece goes above the second

parts.note: a yard is a courtyard, an enclosed court
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A judge decides the length of the sentence the court has imposed.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is all prison sentencing, but 'court' is a yard and 'time' an age.
explanation.definitionFit: Yardage is a distance measured in yards, so it means a length.

clue.text: St Michael in action — he sought a panacea

indicators.note: letters put into action are set moving and rearranged

explanation.surface: The archangel Michael is pictured busily seeking a cure-all.
explanation.definitionFit: Alchemists searched for the elixir of life, a universal remedy or cure-all.

clue.text: Like swelling youth has acquired in the course of climbing

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a lad is a youth
on can mean during or in the course of, as in on the way

explanation.surface: A young man notices a swelling he picked up while out climbing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns the whole of LAD plus ON upwards; 'has acquired' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A node is a swelling or knot, and nodal means relating to or like a node.

clue.text: Deprive of an ear working mechanically

parts.note: to rob someone is to deprive them of something
otic is the medical adjective meaning relating to the ear

explanation.surface: Someone loses an ear and carries on like a machine.
explanation.definitionFit: Robotic describes acting like a robot, stiffly and mechanically.

clue.text: Certainty is only to be expected

definitions.meaning: a sure thing, someone or something certain to succeed
normal or what anyone would expect

explanation.definitionFit: Natural as a noun is a dead cert, and as an adjective means normal or expected.

clue.text: A chink in the armour of hero — and antihero

parts.note: Achilles was the great Greek hero of the Trojan War
a heel is a cad or rotter, a far cry from a hero

explanation.surface: A villain finds the one weak spot in the armour of a heroic figure.
explanation.walkthrough: A heel is a contemptible person, hence the antihero.
explanation.definitionFit: An Achilles heel is an idiom for a single weak point, just as a chink is a gap in armour.

clue.text: Two-thirds of university colleges initially supply linen

indicators.note: only two-thirds of the word is kept, so its last three of nine letters are dropped

parts.note: Cambridge is a famous English university

indicators.note: initially picks out the first letter of the word colleges

explanation.surface: A university's colleges are first to order in a stock of linen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two-thirds of' cuts DGE from CAMBRIDGE, leaving CAMBRI.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambric is a fine, closely woven white linen or cotton fabric.

clue.text: Part taken in action recorded in account

indicators.note: one piece is taken in by the other, enclosed within it

parts.note: a deed is an act or action
a bit is a part or piece

explanation.surface: A bookkeeper notes the part someone played in an action.
explanation.definitionFit: Debited means entered as a charge on the debit side of an account.

clue.text: Eats licensed for distribution here

indicators.note: letters given out for distribution are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A shop that is licensed to hand out food to customers.
explanation.definitionFit: A delicatessen is a shop selling prepared foods, a place where eats are given out.

clue.text: Three consecutive notes follow one that's cut off

indicators.note: the second piece follows, coming after, the first

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
so, la and te are three neighbouring notes of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A singer runs three notes in a row after one that was cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: To isolate is to cut off or separate from others.

clue.text: Misprint — I'll rate its producer

indicators.note: the letters given produce the thing by being reworked, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A proofreader grades whoever made a printing error.
explanation.definitionFit: A literal is a printers' term for a typographical error.

clue.text: Story, say, set round European city

parts.note: a lie is a made-up story

indicators.note: set round means turned about, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: eg (for example) is what say means here

explanation.surface: A tale is set in a European city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Story, say' reads as one idea, but the comma splits it: 'say' is the usual crossword cue for EG, which 'set round' turns about.
explanation.definitionFit: Liège is a city in eastern Belgium.

clue.text: When I climb, ice gets slippery — it's stupid

indicators.note: something slippery slides about, so the letters move into a new order

explanation.surface: A climber notes that it's foolish to go up when the ice is slippery.
explanation.definitionFit: Imbecilic means foolish or idiotic.

clue.text: Fine things perhaps thrown in one Bach composition

indicators.note: a composition puts the letters together in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An object is hurled during a performance of a Bach piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrown' looks like the anagram signal but belongs to the definition: pots are thrown on a wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: Bone china is fine porcelain; fine wares are perhaps thrown on a potter's wheel.

clue.text: Counsellor — man given a female name

parts.note: Sam is a man's name
Rita is a woman's name, standing in for a female

explanation.surface: An adviser, a man, is given a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Samaritans are a charity whose volunteers counsel people in distress, so a Samaritan is such a counsellor.

clue.text: Man, taking motorway, caught woman up

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, read here as MI
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read upwards, backwards

parts.note: Leah is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A man driving on the motorway catches up with a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the London-to-Leeds motorway, with the figure 1 taken as letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Michael is a common masculine given name, so it names one particular man.

clue.text: Cross initially, to some extent he produced harmony

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone angry at first at least makes peace in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Rossini was an Italian composer, a creator of musical harmony.

clue.text: Was first back with paper cups, etc

indicators.note: back means the word is turned backwards

parts.note: led means was in front or first
FT is the Financial Times newspaper

explanation.surface: A newspaper took the lead with a story about trophy cups.
explanation.definitionFit: Delft is glazed earthenware from the Dutch town, used for cups, plates and so on.

clue.text: Energetic policemen round a lot of people up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the whole lot reads upwards, backwards
the police letters go round, enclosing, the other piece

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, Britain's plain-clothes detectives
many means a large number of people

explanation.surface: Lively police officers round up a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like part of the phrase 'round up', but it is the container signal, and 'up' alone reverses everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Dynamic means full of energy and drive.

clue.text: Student of English, a composer, going from side to side

parts.note: L for left is one side
Thomas Arne was the English composer of Rule, Britannia!
R for right is the other side

explanation.surface: A pupil studying English swings between two moods like a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going from side to side' supplies L (left) at one end and R (right) at the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A learner is a student or pupil.

clue.text: Spots return directions for boxes

indicators.note: return means turn back, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: acne is an outbreak of spots
S, E and S are compass directions, south, east, south

explanation.surface: Instructions for packaging come back covered in spots.
explanation.definitionFit: Encases means encloses or boxes in, as a verb.

clue.text: Throttle in car's manipulated to gain acceleration

indicators.note: letters manipulated are worked around into a new order

parts.note: g is the symbol for acceleration due to gravity

explanation.surface: A driver works the throttle in the car to speed up.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrag is to wring the neck of, or throttle.

clue.text: Poll sails south

parts.note: canvas is a ship's sails collectively

explanation.surface: An opinion poll heads south on the sailing.
explanation.definitionFit: To canvass is to poll or seek opinions or votes.

clue.text: Painter represses expression of disgust with still more green

indicators.note: to repress is to hold in, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: Edward Lear was a landscape painter as well as a nonsense poet
fie is an old exclamation of disgust

explanation.surface: An artist stifles his distaste for an even greener landscape.
explanation.definitionFit: Leafier means having more leaves, so greener still.

clue.text: I am pursued by people heading towards Kent in Jumbo

indicators.note: pursued by means followed by, so the later pieces come after

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am
men are people
Kent lies in south-east England, so SE is the direction to head

explanation.surface: Someone is chased by a crowd towards Kent in a jumbo jet.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in the south-east corner of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Jumbo as an adjective means very large, huge or enormous.

clue.text: Phenomenon observed when bull enters china shop?

definitions.text: Phenomenon observed when bull enters china shop?

parts.words: Phenomenon observed when bull enters china shop?
parts.note: read literally, a bull blundering among the crockery sends plates sailing through the air, which also names a sighting of a UFO

explanation.surface: A strange sight when a bull blunders into a crockery shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as an aerial sighting, it is an unidentified craft reported in the sky, here also a hurled plate.
